chunks: Go to Pharaoh and tell him: 'We are messengers of the Lord of the worlds.'

key_terms.رَبِ الْعَالَمِينَ: Lord of the worlds, emphasizing divine authority over all creation

ai.seo_question: What message did Musa and Harun carry to Pharaoh?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Ash-Shu'ara, this verse marks the transition from divine preparation to public confrontation, emphasizing that Musa and Harun (AS) speak with the authority of the 'Lord of the Worlds' rather than their own. Shia exegesis highlights this as a model for da'wah, where messengers address both the elite and the masses with clarity and confidence, rooted in the conviction of Tawhid. The command underscores the prophetic duty to convey the message regardless of the recipient's status or resistance.
